# Programming & Computer-System Knowledge Quiz

[← Optiver](../README.md) · [Every Optiver question](../../optiver.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/coding-knowledge-test)

`cs-fundamentals` `networking` `operating-systems`

---

## Format and scope

- Expect about 20 questions in roughly 20 minutes, combining single-choice and multiple-choice items. In most cases, you cannot go back to an earlier question.
- Topics include networking (TCP/IP, multicast, and fairness), relational databases (normalization), operating systems (scheduling, CPU cores, and process starvation), multithreading, data structures, and interpreting code and its complexity.
- Some candidates report having sufficient time to consult outside resources or GenAI during this section.

## Question examples

Reported prompts, already paraphrased:

- In a relational database, what is meant by “normalization”?
- There is one publisher and many subscribers, each on a distinct host with the same single-NIC configuration, and every subscriber must receive the published data simultaneously. Which delivery approach is most appropriate? (multicast-related)
- A two-core machine runs five identical processes continuously; four receive equal CPU time while the fifth receives none. Which operating-system component accounts for this starvation? (scheduler)
- A program needs to hold distinct words together with their definitions, with entries arriving in arbitrary order. Which data structure suits the stated lookup requirement?
- Examine a brief code fragment and determine its time complexity.

## Observations

- The operating-system and networking items tend to emphasize practical situations—such as scheduling fairness, multicast versus unicast or broadcast, and starvation—instead of obscure facts.
- Keep a strict pace: with 20 questions, 20 minutes, and no ability to revisit items, you have about one minute per question.

## Preparation

- Refresh OS scheduling topics such as starvation, priority, and fairness, along with TCP/IP, multicast fundamentals, and database normalization forms.
- Rehearse identifying Big-O complexity from short code snippets so these questions can be answered immediately.
